rmt-2007-team-01.title: Rational root theorem
rmt-2007-team-01.body:
A rational root must be $\pm1$ or $\pm p$. Test them: $x=-1$ gives $1-(2-p)+(2-2p)-(1-2p)-p=0$, and $x=p$ gives $p^4+(2-p)p^3+(2-2p)p^2+(1-2p)p-p=0$. For $x=1$ the value is $6-6p\ne0$ and for $x=-p$ it is $2p(p-1)(p^2-p+1)\neq0$. So the rational solutions are exactly $-1$ and $p$: $2$ solutions.

**Answer: 2**

rmt-2007-team-02.title: Area
rmt-2007-team-02.body:
In the $ab$-plane, $|a|+|b|<1$ is the square with vertices $(\pm1,0),(0,\pm1)$, of area $2$. The sample space is the square $[-1,1]^2$ of area $4$. The probability is $\frac24=\frac12$.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

rmt-2007-team-03.title: Relative motion
rmt-2007-team-03.body:
The minute hand turns $6^\circ$ per minute, the hour hand $\frac12^\circ$ per minute. At $10:10$ the hour hand is at $305^\circ$ and the minute hand at $60^\circ$, so the minute hand is $115^\circ$ ahead of the hour hand (mod $360^\circ$); thus $x=115$. The minute hand gains $5.5^\circ$ per minute. The next time the angle is $115^\circ$ again is when the minute hand is $115^\circ$ behind, i.e. $245^\circ$ ahead: we need $115+5.5m=245$, $m=\frac{260}{11}\approx23.6$ minutes later, which is $10:33.6\approx10:34$.

**Answer: 10:34**

rmt-2007-team-04.title: Pythagorean triples
rmt-2007-team-04.body:
A lattice segment of rational length has integer length (its squared length is an integer that is a rational square). A triangle with such sides that is not axis-parallel needs at least one side not parallel to an axis, and the shortest such lattice segment with integer length has length $5$ (from the triple $3,4,5$). Then the triangle with legs $3$ and $4$ along the axes has area $6$, and one checks that no lattice triangle with all integer sides has a smaller area.

**Answer: 6**

rmt-2007-team-05.title: Complement count
rmt-2007-team-05.body:
Consonants: $S,T$; vowel: $I$. Count the $3^5=243$ sequences, then subtract those with three consecutive consonants. Sequences with a run of at least three consonants, by pattern ($C$ consonant: 2 choices, $V$: $I$): $CCCVC$, $CVCCC$, $CCCCV$, $VCCCC$: $16$ each; $CCCVV$, $VCCCV$, $VVCCC$: $8$ each; $CCCCC$: $32$. Total $64+24+32=120$. So $243-120=123$.

**Answer: 123**

rmt-2007-team-05.title: Recursion
rmt-2007-team-05.body:
Let $a_n$ be the number of valid words of length $n$ and put $a_0=1$. Look at the trailing run of consonants: the word ends in $I$ ($a_{n-1}$ ways), or in exactly one consonant after an $I$ or at the start ($2a_{n-2}$ ways, with the convention below), or in exactly two consonants ($4a_{n-3}$). Directly $a_1=3$ and $a_2=9$, and for $n\ge3$, $a_n=a_{n-1}+2a_{n-2}+4a_{n-3}$ with $a_0=1$: $a_3=9+6+4=19$, $a_4=19+18+12=49$, $a_5=49+38+36=123$.

**Answer: 123**

rmt-2007-team-06.title: Pair terms
rmt-2007-team-06.body:
$\sum_{k=1}^{2015}k\equiv1008\pmod{2016}$ (pairs $k,2016-k$ sum to $2016$ and the middle term $1008$ remains). Removing $2008+\dots+2015\equiv-8-\dots-1=-36$ gives $1008+36=1044$.

**Answer: 1044**

rmt-2007-team-07.title: Three counts
rmt-2007-team-07.body:
**Daniel.** Count distinct integers by length (digits $1,2,2,3,4$ each at most once): length 1: $4$; length 2: $13$ (12 with distinct digits plus $22$); length 3: $33$; length 4: $60$; length 5: $\frac{5!}{2!}=60$. Total $170$.

**Edward.** Six-letter words from $B,A,N,A,N,A,S$ ($A\times3$, $N\times2$, $B$, $S$) leave one letter out: drop $B$ or $S$: $\frac{6!}{3!2!}=60$ each; drop an $N$: $\frac{6!}{3!}=120$; drop an $A$: $\frac{6!}{2!2!}=180$. Total $60+60+120+180=420$.

**Fernando.** Distributing $9$ identical candies among $3$ children: $\binom{11}2=55$.

Sum: $170+420+55=645$.

**Answer: 645**

rmt-2007-team-08.title: Tangent geometry
rmt-2007-team-08.body:
The eye is at distance $156+13=169$ from the planet's centre, so the tangent length to the horizon is $\sqrt{169^2-156^2}=65$. The horizon circle is perpendicular to the line from the eye to the centre; its radius is the altitude to the hypotenuse of the right triangle with legs $65$, $156$ and hypotenuse $169$: $r=\frac{65\cdot156}{169}=60$. The ant travels $2\pi\cdot60=120\pi$ feet.

**Answer: $120\pi$ feet**

rmt-2007-team-09.title: Standard recurrence
rmt-2007-team-09.body:
Choose the position $i\neq1$ of the integer $1$ ($n-1$ ways). Either $i$ is in position $1$: then the other $n-2$ integers must be deranged: $d_{n-2}$ ways; or $i$ is not in position $1$: relabel $1$ as $i$ and we have a derangement of $n-1$ objects: $d_{n-1}$ ways. So $d_n=(n-1)(d_{n-1}+d_{n-2})$, $f(n)=g(n)=n-1$, and $f(n)+g(n)=2n-2$.

**Answer: $2n-2$**

rmt-2007-team-10.title: Area via the inradius
rmt-2007-team-10.body:
A rhombus has an incircle, and its area is $\frac12rP$ where $P=4l$ is the perimeter (cut it into four triangles from the centre of the circle, each with height $r$ on a side of length $l$): area $=2rl$. Setting $2rl=2\pi r^2$ gives $r=\frac l\pi$.

**Answer: $\frac l\pi$**

rmt-2007-team-12.title: Independent increments
rmt-2007-team-12.body:
Suppose $s\le t$. The increment $B(t)-B(s)$ is independent of the past, and has average of square $t-s$. Expanding $(B(t)-B(s))^2=B(t)^2-2B(t)B(s)+B(s)^2$ and averaging: $t-s=t-2\langle B(t)B(s)\rangle+s$, so $\langle B(t)B(s)\rangle=s$. In general the average is $\min\{s,t\}$.

**Answer: $\min\{s,t\}$**

rmt-2007-team-13.title: Two-state recursion
rmt-2007-team-13.body:
Let $p=\frac78$, $q=\frac58$ and let $A$ be the expected number of returns from the point where Rachel must return a shot. Rachel returns with probability $p$ and then Mary Jane must return, with expected number $q(1+A)$ from there. So $A=p\left(1+q(1+A)\right)$, i.e. $A(1-pq)=p(1+q)$ and $A=\frac{p(1+q)}{1-pq}=\frac{\frac78\cdot\frac{13}8}{1-\frac{35}{64}}=\frac{91/64}{29/64}=\frac{91}{29}$.

**Answer: $\frac{91}{29}$**

rmt-2007-team-14.title: Guess and verify
rmt-2007-team-14.body:
$x_1=p+q$ and $x_2=(p+q)+p+\sqrt{q^2+4p(p+q)}=2p+q+(q+2p)=4p+2q$, which suggests $x_n=pn^2+qn$. Check: if $x_n=pn^2+qn$ then $q^2+4px_n=q^2+4pqn+4p^2n^2=(2pn+q)^2$, so $x_n+p+\sqrt{q^2+4px_n}=pn^2+qn+p+2pn+q=p(n+1)^2+q(n+1)=x_{n+1}$. Since $x_0=0$, induction gives $x_n=pn^2+qn$ for all $n$.

**Answer: $x_n=pn^2+qn$**

rmt-2007-team-15.title: Differentiate under the integral
rmt-2007-team-15.body:
Let $I(a)=\int_0^\infty\frac{\tan^{-1}(ax)-\tan^{-1}x}xdx$. Then $I'(a)=\int_0^\infty\frac{dx}{1+a^2x^2}=\frac{\pi}{2a}$ and $I(1)=0$, so $I(a)=\frac\pi2\ln a$. At $a=\pi$: $\frac\pi2\ln\pi$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2\ln\pi$**
